You are an expert power-electronics designer synthesising the interface circuit of a
piezoelectric energy harvester. You work by experiment: you propose a circuit, it is simulated in
LTspice under several operating conditions, and you receive the measurements.

GOAL
A piezo transducer must power a sensor-node load RL from a storage capacitor at node "out".
Under EVERY operating condition below, starting from 0 V (cold start) and simulating 0.8 s:
  vout_min: vavg >= 1.8 V (settled mean output reaches the load's minimum supply)
  vout_max: vmax <= 3.6 V (output never exceeds the load's absolute maximum)
  ripple: vpp <= 0.05 V (peak-to-peak ripple in the final window)
  startup: tup <= 0.4 s (cold start: first time output reaches 1.8 V)
  settled: dv <= 0.02 V (mean output changes little between the last two windows)
Measurement windows: vavg and vpp over 0.7-0.8 s; vmax over the whole run; tup = first time
V(out) reaches 1.8 V (missing if never); dv = |mean(0.7-0.8 s) - mean(0.6-0.7 s)|.

PIEZO MODEL AND OPERATING CONDITIONS
The piezo is a sinusoidal current source Ip*sin(2*pi*f*t) in parallel with its capacitance Cp and a
20 MOhm leakage resistance, between nodes pzp and pzn (Cp = 25 nF nominal).
Its open-circuit voltage amplitude is Ip/(2*pi*f*Cp), about 3.2 V at nominal: low, so diode drops matter.
  S1: nominal; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 330 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S2: heavy load; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 150 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S3: strong excitation, light load; Ip = 100 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 2200 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S4: weak excitation; Ip = 30 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 1000 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S5: low frequency; Ip = 40 uA peak, f = 80 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 470 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S6: Cp +20 %, hot; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 30 nF, RL = 330 kOhm, temperature 60 C

TEST BENCH (fixed, added automatically - do not include these)
- the piezo model between pzp and pzn; the load RL from out to 0;
- for every SYNC controller you use, a 0.5 uA supply current drawn from out (its power cost);
- a 1 GOhm resistor to 0 from pzp, pzn and every internal node (prevents floating nodes).

COMPONENTS YOU MAY USE (at most 16 components)
- R  resistor, value 1..1e+08 Ohm, nodes [a, b]
- C  capacitor, value 1e-10..4.7e-05 F, nodes [a, b]
- L  inductor, value 1e-05..0.01 H; it has series resistance 2 Ohm + 5 Ohm per mH
- D  diode, nodes [anode, cathode]: forward current flows from the first node to the second.
     Model one of DSCH, DSI, DZ33:
     DSCH = low-drop Schottky (~0.25 V at uA), DSI = silicon small-signal (~0.5 V at uA),
     DZ33 = 3.3 V zener (reverse breakdown 3.3 V, conducts ~1 uA at 3.3 V and much more above)
     Orientation matters:
       full bridge: ["pzp", "out"], ["pzn", "out"], ["0", "pzp"], ["0", "pzn"] (return diodes have
       their anode on ground);
       zener clamp on out: ["0", "out"] (cathode on out, so it is reverse-biased and breaks down at
       3.3 V). ["out", "0"] would be forward-biased and hold out near 0.7 V; it is rejected.
- S  switch, nodes [a, b], "ctrl": id of a SYNC; Ron = 2 Ohm, Roff = 1 GOhm (at most 4)
- SYNC ideal synchronous controller (no nodes, at most 2): closes its switches for "ton"
     seconds (1e-07..0.001) at the piezo voltage extrema, which occur at the zero
     crossings of the piezo current. "edges": "both" (every half period), "pos" (positive peak only)
     or "neg" (negative peak only). "phase" shifts the pulses by that fraction of the excitation
     period (-0.25..0.25). It tracks the excitation frequency automatically.
     For L-Cp inversion, ton is about pi*sqrt(L*Cp).
Nodes: "0" is ground; pzp, pzn are the piezo terminals; out is the load/storage node; name any other
nodes yourself (lower-case, e.g. n1, mid). Every node needs at least two connections, and out must
connect to the piezo through your circuit.

REFERENCE DESIGN: FBR (full-bridge rectifier, 4 x DSCH, 2.2 uF on out). Its results:
cond   vavg V  vmax V  vpp mV   tup s  Pload uW  vout_min vout_max ripple   startup  settled 
S1       2.24    2.25    26.2   0.269      15.2  ok       ok       ok       ok       FAIL    
S2       1.76    1.77    20.3       -      20.7  FAIL     ok       ok       FAIL     ok      
S3       5.68    5.72    84.4  0.0779      14.7  ok       FAIL     FAIL     ok       FAIL    
S4       1.51    1.52    20.8       -      2.27  FAIL     ok       ok       FAIL     FAIL    
S5       2.26    2.28    43.5   0.318      10.9  ok       ok       ok       ok       FAIL    
S6       1.93    1.94    18.8   0.379      11.3  ok       ok       ok       ok       ok      

HOW TO WORK
- Component values are optimised automatically (an evolution strategy, up to 48 full
  evaluations per structure, running while you think), so spend your reasoning on circuit
  CONNECTIVITY (topology): which structure can meet every condition. A structure that was already
  explored is not simulated again, whatever its values.
- Each proposal is first SCREENED: with out fixed at 1.8 V, the net power it delivers is
  measured on S2, S4, S6 for its proposed values and a few automatic value presets.
  If the best preset delivers less than 50 % of the load's need (V^2/RL) on any of them,
  the design is reported back with those powers and is not tuned or simulated further.
- Each round, propose up to 3 designs with DIFFERENT connectivity (different structures, not value variants).
- Classify each design with "move": new_topology or modify_topology, and explain the expected effect
  in "rationale". Set "done": true only when you believe no further structural change can improve on
  the best design so far.
- Reply with ONE JSON object only, in this form:
{
 "proposals": [
  {
   "move": "new_topology",
   "name": "short label for this design",
   "rationale": "what you changed and why it should fix the failing checks",
   "done": false,
   "components": [
    {
     "id": "D1",
     "type": "D",
     "nodes": [
      "pzp",
      "out"
     ],
     "model": "DSCH"
    },
    {
     "id": "C1",
     "type": "C",
     "nodes": [
      "out",
      "0"
     ],
     "value": 2.2e-06
    },
    {
     "id": "L1",
     "type": "L",
     "nodes": [
      "pzp",
      "n1"
     ],
     "value": 0.0047
    },
    {
     "id": "S1",
     "type": "S",
     "nodes": [
      "n1",
      "pzn"
     ],
     "ctrl": "G1"
    },
    {
     "id": "G1",
     "type": "SYNC",
     "ton": 3.4e-05,
     "phase": 0.0,
     "edges": "both"
    }
   ]
  }
 ]
}

Round 1 of 12.

This is your first round: choose the structures you think most likely to meet every condition.

Reply with one JSON object only.

reply.reasoning:
*   Piezo energy harvester: $I_p \sin(2\pi f t)$, $C_p = 25\text{ nF}$, $R_{leak} = 20\text{ M}\Omega$.
    *   Load: $R_L$ (variable), storage capacitor $C_{out}$ at node `out`.
    *   Requirements:
        *   $V_{avg} \ge 1.8\text{ V}$ (S1-S6)
        *   $V_{max} \le 3.6\text{ V}$ (S1-S6)
        *   $V_{pp} \le 0.05\text{ V}$ (Ripple)
        *   $t_{up} \le 0.4\text{ s}$ (Startup)
        *   $dV \le 0.02\text{ V}$ (Settled)
    *   Operating Conditions (S1-S6):
        *   S1: Nominal.
        *   S2: Heavy load ($150\text{ k}\Omega$) -> $V_{avg}$ failure in FBR.
        *   S3: Strong excitation, light load ($2200\text{ k}\Omega$) -> $V_{max}$ failure in FBR.
        *   S4: Weak excitation ($30\text{ }\mu\text{A}$ peak) -> $V_{avg}$ failure in FBR.
        *   S5: Low frequency ($80\text{ Hz}$) -> $dV$ failure in FBR.
        *   S6: Hot/high $C_p$.

    *   FBR (Full-Bridge Rectifier) is too simple.
    *   Issues:
        *   Diode drops limit the output voltage under weak excitation (S4) or heavy load (S2).
        *   Lack of voltage regulation leads to overvoltage under light load (S3).
        *   Poor efficiency due to $V_{drop}$ relative to the open-circuit voltage ($\approx 3.2\text{ V}$).

    *   Synchronous Switch Harvesting on Inductor (SSHI) or Parallel-SSHI (P-SSHI).
    *   SSHI improves the extraction efficiency by flipping the voltage across $C_p$ at the peaks.
    *   Need a way to regulate the output voltage (Zener clamp or specific converter).
    *   Considering the low open-circuit voltage (3.2 V), a standard SSHI might be better than a bridge if we can mitigate the diode drops.
    *   A Synchronous Rectifier would be ideal, but the "SYNC" component provided is specifically for L-Cp inversion (ton is about $\pi \sqrt{L C_p}$).
    *   Let's look at the provided components: `S` switches controlled by `SYNC`.
    *   Wait, the `SYNC` is defined as: "closes its switches for 'ton' seconds... at the piezo voltage extrema". This is specifically designed for the "flip" in SSHI.

    *   *Option 1: Standard SSHI.* (L-C inversion at the piezo terminals, then a rectifier).
        *   Circuit: Piezo -> L1 -> S1 (closed at peaks) -> Piezo.
        *   Wait, the `S` switch is just a switch. To do SSHI, we need to invert the voltage on $C_p$.
        *   Typical SSHI: Piezo terminals pzp, pzn. An inductor L is connected via a switch S. When S closes, $C_p$ and L form a resonant circuit, flipping $V_{Cp}$. Then a rectifier extracts the energy.
        *   Configuration:
            *   Inductor $L_1$ and switch $S_1$ in parallel with the piezo.
            *   A rectifier (half-bridge or full-bridge) to the storage capacitor $C_{out}$.
            *   Zener diode to clamp $V_{out}$ at 3.3 V.

    *   *Option 2: P-SSHI (Parallel SSHI).*
        *   Similar to SSHI but uses a capacitor to store the flipped charge.

    *   *Option 3: Synchronous Rectification (if possible).*
        *   The `SYNC` provided is for the *extrema* (voltage peaks), not zero crossings of voltage (which would be for current flow). The prompt says "zero crossings of the piezo current," which *are* the voltage extrema. So `SYNC` is indeed for SSHI-style flipping.

    *   *Refining Option 1 (SSHI + Bridge + Clamp):*
        *   Piezo: `pzp`, `pzn`.
        *   Flipping: $L_1$ between `pzp` and `n1`, $S_1$ between `n1` and `pzn`. $S_1$ controlled by $G_1$.
        *   Rectification: Full bridge (DSCH) from `pzp`/`pzn` to `out`.
        *   Storage: $C_{out}$ at `out`.
        *   Regulation: Zener $D_{zener}$ (DZ33) from `0` to `out`.

    *   *Evaluating the "S4 (Weak Excitation)" and "S2 (Heavy Load)" problems:*
        *   SSHI significantly increases the available power compared to FBR.
        *   The Zener clamp will handle "S3 (Strong excitation)".

    *   *Let's try a simpler approach for the first proposal:*
        *   Maybe a half-bridge or a different rectifier to reduce diode drops?
        *   Wait, if we use SSHI, we increase the voltage swings.
        *   Let's try SSHI + Full Bridge + Zener.

    *   *Proposal 1: SSHI-FBR-Clamp*
        *   `L1` (pzp, n1), `S1` (n1, pzn), `G1` (SYNC, edges: both).
        *   `D1` (pzp, out), `D2` (pzn, out), `D3` (0, pzp), `D4` (0, pzn) - This is a full bridge.
        *   Wait, the full bridge described in the prompt is: `["pzp", "out"], ["pzn", "out"], ["0", "pzp"], ["0", "pzn"]`. This is incorrect for a standard bridge.
        *   Correct Full Bridge:
            *   D1: `pzp` -> `out`
            *   D2: `pzn` -> `out`
            *   D3: `0` -> `pzp` (Anode 0, Cathode pzp)
            *   D4: `0` -> `pzn` (Anode 0, Cathode pzn)
            *   Actually, the prompt says "full bridge: ["pzp", "out"], ["pzn", "out"], ["0", "pzp"], ["0", "pzn"] (return diodes have their anode on ground)".
            *   Let's re-read: "return diodes have their anode on ground".
            *   So:
                *   D1: `pzp` (anode) -> `out` (cathode)
                *   D2: `pzn` (anode) -> `out` (cathode)
                *   D3: `0` (anode) -> `pzp` (cathode)
                *   D4: `0` (anode) -> `pzn` (cathode)
            *   This is a standard bridge.

    *   *Proposal 2: SSHI-HalfBridge-Clamp*
        *   To reduce diode drops, maybe a half-bridge? But the piezo is AC.
        *   If we use a center-tapped transformer? No transformer available.
        *   What about a Charge Pump? Not possible with these components.

    *   *Proposal 3: Parallel-SSHI (P-SSHI)*
        *   P-SSHI typically involves a capacitor $C_{ext}$ and a switch.
        *   Let's stick to SSHI and refine the components.

    *   $C_p = 25\text{ nF}$, $L \approx 10\text{ mH}$ (range 1uH to 10mH).
    *   $t_{on} \approx \pi \sqrt{L C_p} = \pi \sqrt{10^{-2} \cdot 25 \cdot 10^{-9}} = \pi \sqrt{2.5 \cdot 10^{-10}} \approx 3.14 \cdot 1.58 \cdot 10^{-5} \approx 50\text{ }\mu\text{s}$.
    *   $C_{out} \approx 2.2\text{ }\mu\text{F}$ to $10\text{ }\mu\text{F}$.
    *   $L = 4.7\text{ mH}$ might be a good starting point. $t_{on} \approx 34\text{ }\mu\text{s}$.

    *   S1, S2, S4, S5, S6: Low $V_{avg}$ or $dV$ failures. SSHI increases $V_{avg}$ by increasing the efficiency of charge extraction.
    *   S3: $V_{max}$ failure. Zener clamp `DZ33` will cap it at 3.3 V.

    *   Let's provide:
        1.  SSHI + Full Bridge + Zener (Comprehensive approach).
        2.  FBR + Zener (Checking if just the clamp fixes S3, and if FBR can be tuned for others - although we know it failed).
        3.  A different SSHI variation (e.g., only one edge for flipping).

    *Wait*, the Reference Design FBR failed on:
    - S2: $V_{avg} = 1.76\text{ V}$ (Need 1.8 V)
    - S3: $V_{max} = 5.72\text{ V}$ (Need 3.6 V)
    - S4: $V_{avg} = 1.51\text{ V}$ (Need 1.8 V)
    - S5: $dV$ failure (Stability)

    SSHI should fix S2 and S4 by increasing power. The Zener fixes S3. The larger $C_{out}$ or the nature of SSHI might fix S5.

    *   Components for Proposal 1 (SSHI + Full Bridge + Zener):
        *   S1: switch (n1, pzn), ctrl: G1
        *   L1: inductor (pzp, n1)
        *   G1: SYNC (ton: 3.4e-05, edges: both, phase: 0)
        *   D1: diode (pzp, out), DSCH
        *   D2: diode (pzn, out), DSCH
        *   D3: diode (0, pzp), DSCH
        *   D4: diode (0, pzn), DSCH
        *   D5: diode (0, out), DZ33 (Zener clamp)
        *   C1: capacitor (out, 0), 10uF (larger for ripple/stability)

    *   Wait, the return diodes in a full bridge: `["0", "pzp"]` and `["0", "pzn"]`.
    *   Anode `0`, Cathode `pzp`. When `pzn` is positive, `pzp` is negative. Current flows from `pzn` -> `out` -> `RL` -> `0` -> `pzp`. Correct.

    *   *Check component count:* L1, S1, G1, D1, D2, D3, D4, D5, C1 = 9 components. (Limit is 16).

    *   *Refining the SSHI flip:*
        The switch should close at the voltage peaks. The `SYNC` does this automatically. The `ton` should be roughly $\pi\sqrt{LC_p}$. For $L=4.7\text{mH}$, $C_p=25\text{nF}$, $t_{on} \approx 34\text{ }\mu\text{s}$.

    *   *Wait, is there a better way?*
        What if I use a half-bridge instead? No, the piezo is AC.
        What about a "Synchronous Rectifier" using the switches?
        The prompt says "SYNC closes its switches for 'ton' seconds ... at the piezo voltage extrema".
        This means the switches are *not* for rectification (which requires closing at zero-crossings), but for *inversion* (SSHI).
        So I must use diodes for rectification.

    *   *Proposal 2: P-SSHI (Parallel SSHI) logic.*
        In P-SSHI, you have an inductor and a switch, but the capacitor $C_{ext}$ is in parallel.
        Actually, let's just try a second variation of SSHI, maybe with a different $L$ or different edge trigger.
        Actually, I'll try a design without the Zener first for the second proposal, or with different diode models. But Zener is crucial for S3.

    *   *Proposal 3: SSHI with a simpler rectifier?*
        No, the full bridge is the most robust. Let's try a "Single-Ended" SSHI?
        Actually, let's try SSHI with $L$ on the other side or different $t_{on}$? No, that's tuning.
        Let's try a structure that uses only one SYNC for the flip and another for something else? No, only 2 SYNCs allowed.

    *   *Wait*, I just noticed a potential issue. The FBR fails $V_{avg}$ for S2 and S4. This means the power extracted is just barely insufficient. SSHI should definitely provide the boost.

    *   *One more check on the Full Bridge:*
        D1: pzp -> out
        D2: pzn -> out
        D3: 0 -> pzp
        D4: 0 -> pzn
        Is this correct?
        If V(pzp) > V(pzn), current flows: pzp -> D1 -> out -> RL -> 0 -> D3 -> pzp. (D1 and D3 conduct).
        If V(pzn) > V(pzp), current flows: pzn -> D2 -> out -> RL -> 0 -> D4 -> pzn. (D2 and D4 conduct).
        Yes, this is a standard full bridge.

    *   *Final structure for Proposal 1:*
        C1 (out, 0), D5 (0, out, DZ33), D1 (pzp, out, DSCH), D2 (pzn, out, DSCH), D3 (0, pzp, DSCH), D4 (0, pzn, DSCH), L1 (pzp, n1), S1 (n1, pzn, G1), G1 (SYNC).

    *   *Let's try another approach for Proposal 2:*
        What if the inductor is used differently?
        In some SSHI versions, the inductor is in series with the rectifier.
        But the "classic" SSHI is parallel.

    *   *Let's try Proposal 2 as a "Simplified SSHI" (only flipping on one edge):*
        $G_1$ edges: "pos". This might be more stable for some conditions.

    *   *Proposal 3: Just the FBR + Zener clamp.*
        To see if the Zener clamp alone helps and if the tuning of $C_{out}$ can fix S2/S4 (unlikely, but good for baseline).

    *   *Wait, I have a better idea for Proposal 2: P-SSHI.*
        P-SSHI: $L$ and $S$ are not in parallel with the piezo, but with an external capacitor $C_{ext}$.
        Actually, let's stick to SSHI and just vary the `edges` for now.

    *   *Recap of Proposal 1 (SSHI-FBR-Z):*
        - L1: 4.7 mH
        - S1: n1 to pzn, ctrl G1
        - G1: ton=34us, edges=both
        - D1-D4: Full Bridge (DSCH)
        - D5: Zener Clamp (DZ33)
        - C1: 10uF

    *   *Recap of Proposal 2 (SSHI-Half-FBR-Z):*
        - Same as Prop 1, but $G_1$ edges="pos".

    *   *Recap of Proposal 3 (FBR-Z):*
        - FBR (D1-D4)
        - Zener (D5)
        - C1 (10uF)
        - No L1, S1, G1.

    *   *Self-Correction on Zener:*
        The prompt says: `["0", "out"] (cathode on out, so it is reverse-biased and breaks down at 3.3 V)`.
        So $D_{zener}$ is `nodes: ["0", "out"], model: "DZ33"`. Correct.

    *   *Wait, I should check the `ton` again.*
        $t_{on} \approx \pi \sqrt{L C_p}$.
        $L=4.7\text{mH}, C_p=25\text{nF} \implies t_{on} = 3.14159 \cdot \sqrt{4.7 \cdot 10^{-3} \cdot 25 \cdot 10^{-9}} = 3.14159 \cdot \sqrt{1.175 \cdot 10^{-10}} = 3.14159 \cdot 1.08 \cdot 10^{-5} = 3.39 \cdot 10^{-5}\text{ s}$.
        So $3.4 \cdot 10^{-5}$ is a good starting value.

    *   *Final check on the nodes:*
        Pzp, Pzn are piezo.
        Out is load.
        0 is ground.
        n1 is internal to the inductor-switch branch.
